Custom Bathroom Remodeling in Cary, NC

Plan a bathroom that works for your daily routine, with design consultation, material selection and installation from The Bath Remodeling Center in Cary. We help homeowners in Cary, Raleigh and Apex plan custom vanities, tile, showers, tubs, fixtures and finishes as part of a coordinated bathroom renovation.

Start with your goals: a better shower layout, more practical storage, updated finishes or a complete primary bathroom remodel. Explore our bathroom remodeling services and Cary design showroom to see how your ideas can take shape.

Why Choose The Bath Remodeling Center For Your Home?

Compare more than finishes when choosing a bathroom remodeler. Look at completed work, how the design is developed and what the installation plan includes. Our before-and-after bathroom gallery lets you explore real projects, while our remodeling process explains the steps from planning to completion.

At our Cary showroom, you can compare tile, cabinetry, countertops and fixtures in person. Bring photos of your current bathroom and a list of what you want to change so the conversation starts with your needs. Contact our remodeling team to discuss your project.

The Bath Remodeling Center provides bathroom design and renovation services from our Cary, NC showroom. Our work includes design consultation, custom cabinetry, tile, fixtures and finishes. See our bath remodeling options to begin planning your space.

Plan the Bathroom Around How You Use It
Primary and Master Bathroom Remodeling

Start with the layout, not just the color palette. Think about the space around the vanity, how the shower opens, where towels belong and whether the existing tub fits your routine. Bring these priorities to your consultation so storage, fixture placement and finish selections can be considered together.

Showers, Tubs and Tile

Compare the shower enclosure, wall and floor finishes, fixtures and cleaning needs as a complete design. Our service options include frameless showers, tubs and a range of tile selections. In the bathroom showroom, you can see materials in person and discuss how different choices could work in your home.

Vanities, Storage and Finishing Details

A custom vanity is an opportunity to improve both storage and daily use. Consider drawer space, countertop room and how the doors open within your layout. Coordinate cabinetry, mirrors, faucets and other finishes before finalizing the design rather than making each selection in isolation.

From Initial Ideas to a Remodeling Plan
Describe what needs to change. Share photos of the room, the features you want to keep and the problems you want the remodel to solve.
Explore design and material options. Use the showroom to compare tile, fixtures, cabinetry and finishes alongside your project goals.
Review the proposed scope. Discuss what is included, how selections affect the estimate and the expected installation sequence before work begins.

Read our bathroom remodeling process for more detail. Your initial home visit and first showroom appointment are offered at no cost, along with a complimentary remodeling estimate. More extensive consultations beyond those initial steps may involve consultation fees.

Questions to Bring to Your Bathroom Consultation
What affects the cost of a bathroom remodel?

The size of the room is only one factor. A change to the layout, the scope of plumbing or electrical work, cabinetry, tile and fixture selections can all affect the estimate. Identify your must-have improvements first, then discuss alternatives with the team before approving the scope.

How should I prepare for a showroom appointment?

Bring photos, approximate room dimensions if available, a list of your priorities and examples of styles you like. Let the team know if ease of access, storage, cleaning or keeping a bathtub is especially important. These details help make the consultation specific to your household.

Can I see examples of completed work?

Yes. Browse our completed bathroom transformations and customer reviews. Look for projects with layouts or features similar to yours, then bring those examples to the discussion.

We serve Cary, Raleigh, Apex and other communities listed on our service-area page. Request a bathroom remodeling consultation with your location and the changes you have in mind.

About
Our Team: Your Bath Remodeling Experts
 

At The Bath Remodeling Center, we are passionate about transforming bathrooms into stunning, functional spaces that exceed our customers’ expectations. With over 25 years of experience in the industry, our expert team brings creativity, craftsmanship, and attention to detail to every project we undertake. From concept to completion, we work closely with our clients to understand their vision and deliver customized solutions that suit their needs and style preferences. Whether it’s a small update or a complete overhaul, we take pride in our commitment to quality and customer satisfaction. Trust us to turn your bathroom dreams into reality.

OWNER
Nicole Fella

Nicole Fella is a seasoned professional in the realm of interior design and construction, with a passion for transforming spaces into exquisite works of art. Having graduated from the prestigious Fashion Institute of Technology (F.I.T.) in New York with a degree in Interior Design, Nicole honed her skills and expertise in creating aesthetically pleasing and functional environments.

With a dedication to excellence, Nicole pursued further qualifications and became a NASCLA Licensed General Contractor, demonstrating her commitment to mastering every aspect of the construction process. Over the past 11 years, she has been an integral part of The Bath Remodeling Center,LLC.  where her talent and leadership have contributed significantly to the company’s success.

Now, as the proud owner of The Bath Remodeling Center, LLC. Nicole brings her wealth of experience and creative vision to every project. With an unwavering commitment to customer satisfaction and a keen eye for detail, she leads her team in delivering exceptional results that exceed clients’ expectations.

Nicole’s innovative approach to design, combined with her expertise in construction, allows her to transform ordinary spaces into extraordinary havens that reflect her clients’ unique tastes and lifestyles. Her dedication to quality craftsmanship and personalized service sets her apart in the industry, making her a trusted partner for those seeking to elevate their living spaces to new heights.

At the end of the day, we believe that everyone deserves to have a bathroom they absolutely love. Simply put, we’re the bathroom remodeling experts you can trust to get the job done right, leaving you with a bathroom you’ll enjoy for many years to come!

Explore Your Bathroom Remodeling Options
Bathroom Design, Selections and Installation

A bathroom remodel should solve the problems you experience every day. That may mean replacing a cramped shower, making room for two people at the vanity or organizing storage so the countertop stays clear. The Bath Remodeling Center brings design planning, material selection and installation together for homeowners in Cary, Raleigh and Apex.

Start by telling us what works in your current bathroom and what does not. We can discuss the layout, product choices and installation scope together rather than asking you to choose finishes before the room has a plan.

Custom Showers and Bathing Areas

Consider how you enter the shower, where the controls sit, which products need storage and how the enclosure opens. Our bathroom options include frameless showers, tubs, shower valves and glass and porcelain tile selections. Comparing these features as a complete bathing area helps you choose a design that fits both the room and your routine.

If you are considering replacing a tub with a shower, discuss the space, existing connections and whether the household still needs a bathtub. A larger shower is useful only when the remaining room also works. Bring up access needs early so entry design, clearances and fixture placement can be considered in the plan.

Vanities, Countertops and Useful Storage

Custom-built vanities can address storage needs that a standard cabinet does not. Think about drawers for everyday items, space for towels and the location of the sink and plumbing. A double vanity should leave usable counter space and comfortable room to move, rather than simply adding a second sink.

Compare cabinetry with countertop and faucet selections before finalizing the design. The showroom offers a place to see materials together and discuss how finishes, hardware and storage choices will work in your bathroom.

Tile, Fixtures and Comfort Features

Flooring, wall tile, fixtures and accessories should be selected for daily use as well as appearance. Ask about cleaning needs, grout lines and finish coordination. Features such as heated floors can be considered during planning so their installation requirements are included in the scope.

Our bathroom showroom in Cary includes tile, cabinetry, plumbing fixtures and shower enclosure displays. Bring photos of the existing space and examples of styles you like to make the visit more productive.

Plan the Scope Before Choosing Every Finish
Keep or change the layout: Identify whether the existing shower, toilet and vanity locations meet your needs.
Set practical priorities: Separate essential changes from optional upgrades so the design can follow your budget.
Coordinate selections: Review tile, cabinets, countertops and fixtures together, including any items still covered by allowances.
Review the written plan: Confirm included work, installation details, exclusions and how requested changes will be handled.

Read our bathroom remodeling process for more about working with the design and installation team. For budgeting questions, our master bathroom remodel cost guide explains project scopes and the items to compare in an estimate.

See the Work Before Planning Your Own Remodel

Use our before-and-after bathroom gallery to compare layouts, cabinetry, tile and shower designs. Note which details solve a problem similar to yours, then bring those examples to your consultation. A project photo is a useful design reference; the same result in another home may require different preparation or installation work.

You can also read customer reviews and learn about The Bath Remodeling Center before discussing your project. We serve Cary, Raleigh, Apex and other listed communities; check our service areas or contact us with your address to confirm availability.

Questions to Resolve Before Construction
How long will my bathroom be unavailable?

Ask for the anticipated construction schedule for your specific scope and clarify when the bathroom will be out of use. Design, selections and product ordering happen separately from on-site installation. Layout changes, material availability and conditions discovered during the work can affect the sequence, so confirm the schedule before arranging access to another bathroom.

Should I purchase fixtures before the design is complete?

Discuss proposed products with the team before ordering. Dimensions, connections and installation requirements must fit the plan. Confirm who supplies each item, when it is needed and how substitutions will be handled before committing to a purchase.

What information helps with the first conversation?

Share your location, photos of the room, the changes you want most and your budget and scheduling goals. Mention any known leaks, damaged finishes or access concerns so they can be discussed during the assessment.

Work closely with an Interior Designer and Licensed General Contractor who will guide you through every design decision, from layout to material selections. Our dedicated full-time employees handle all installations, ensuring consistent, high-quality results across every project. When you work with us, you can expect a personalized and professional experience. Our team will work with you to understand your vision and bring it to life. We will take the time to listen to your needs and preferences and help you select the perfect materials for your bathroom.

Ready to Transform Your Bathroom? Contact Us Today!

Call us today at 919-636-6958 or fill out the form below to get started on your bath remodeling project! Be sure to view our project gallery for hundreds of photos of our finished jobs and read our reviews to get started. 

Your initial home visit and the first showroom appointment come at no cost, and we will provide you with a complimentary estimate for your bathroom remodeling project. For more extensive consultations beyond these initial steps, there may be applicable consultation fees.

Prepare for Your Design and Planning Appointment

Bring photos of your existing bathroom, the features you want to keep or change, and your budget and scheduling priorities. Review our bathroom remodeling services to compare shower, vanity, tile and comfort options before choosing individual finishes.

Clarify the scope: Discuss whether the layout stays in place and which fixtures or surfaces will be replaced.
Confirm selections: Identify the products already chosen and any allowances or decisions still outstanding.
Review the schedule: Ask when the bathroom will be unavailable and whether shower-glass installation or other finishing work occurs later.
Understand changes: Confirm how unexpected conditions, substitutions and added work will be discussed and approved.

For help reviewing a proposal, see our bathroom remodeling budget and estimate guide. Then contact our team with your location and project goals.

Accessible Bathroom Design Tips for Aging in Place

 

 

For many homeowners in Durham and the surrounding Triangle area, staying in a familiar home for as long as possible is an important goal. But as mobility, balance, and daily routines change with age, certain areas of the home can become more difficult to navigate—especially the bathroom.

A thoughtfully designed bathroom can make everyday tasks easier while reducing common safety concerns and maintaining the look and comfort of the space. The best aging-in-place bathroom designs don’t have to feel institutional or overly clinical. With the right layout, fixtures, surfaces, and storage, homeowners can create a bathroom that is both stylish and easier to use for years to come.

If you’re considering a bathroom remodel in Durham, Chapel Hill, Hillsborough, Cary, Raleigh, or another nearby Triangle community, these accessible bathroom design ideas are worth considering.

 

1. Consider a Low-Threshold or Walk-In Shower

Traditional bathtub-shower combinations require users to step over a relatively high tub wall, which can become more difficult as balance and mobility change.

Replacing a tub with a walk-in or low-threshold shower can create easier access while also giving the bathroom a more open, modern appearance.

For homeowners planning ahead, consider creating a shower with enough room to comfortably move around and potentially accommodate a shower chair in the future. A handheld showerhead can also make bathing easier while providing greater flexibility.

These features can be incorporated into a custom design without sacrificing style. Homeowners can explore shower layouts, tile, fixtures, and other materials at The Bath Remodeling Center’s Cary bathroom showroom.

 

2. Add Grab Bars in Strategic Locations

Grab bars are one of the simplest ways to add additional support in a bathroom.

The CDC recommends installing grab bars inside and outside the tub or shower and near the toilet as part of making a home safer for older adults. Falls remain a major concern as people age, and bathroom modifications are one way homeowners can help reduce common hazards. Learn more about fall prevention for older adults from the CDC.

Modern grab bars are available in a wide variety of finishes and designs, so they don’t necessarily need to look like equipment from a hospital or medical facility. Many can coordinate with faucets, shower fixtures, towel bars, and other bathroom hardware.

Even homeowners who don’t need grab bars today may want to consider adding the proper wall reinforcement during a bathroom remodel so bars can be installed more easily later.

 

3. Choose Slip-Resistant Flooring

Bathroom floors are frequently exposed to water, making the flooring selection particularly important in an aging-in-place bathroom.

Consider flooring and shower tile with good traction, particularly when wet. Large transitions between rooms or raised thresholds can also create potential tripping hazards, so a smoother transition between the bathroom and adjoining spaces may make the room easier to navigate.

The goal is to combine safety with design. Today’s porcelain and ceramic tile options make it possible to create a sophisticated bathroom while still prioritizing practical considerations like traction, durability, and ease of maintenance.

 

4. Improve Bathroom Lighting

Good lighting becomes increasingly important as we age.

A bathroom should provide sufficient illumination for showering, grooming, navigating the space at night, and distinguishing changes in floor level or surfaces. The CDC specifically recommends brighter lighting as one way to help make homes safer for older adults.

Consider combining overhead lighting with task lighting around the vanity and shower area. Night lighting or motion-activated lighting can also make nighttime bathroom trips easier.

During a complete bathroom remodel, lighting can be incorporated into the design from the beginning rather than treated as an afterthought.

 

5. Think About the Height of the Toilet

Standard toilets may feel low for someone who has difficulty bending or standing.

A comfort-height toilet can make sitting down and standing back up easier for many adults. Depending on the homeowner’s individual needs, nearby grab bars or additional support may also be useful.

Because accessibility needs vary considerably from person to person, it’s helpful to think about who will use the bathroom now as well as who may use it in the future.

 

6. Make the Vanity Easier to Use

Aging-in-place bathroom design extends beyond showers and toilets.

Vanity height, cabinet placement, countertop space, and storage can all affect how comfortable the room is to use. Frequently used items should be easy to reach without excessive bending, stretching, or climbing.

Drawers can sometimes make bathroom storage more accessible than deep cabinets because users can see and reach items more easily.

The Bath Remodeling Center offers custom cabinetry and other bathroom design options, allowing homeowners to create a vanity configuration suited to their lifestyle and available space. You can see examples and design options in the company’s showroom gallery.

 

7. Consider Wider, More Open Layouts

One of the advantages of planning for aging in place during a full bathroom renovation is the opportunity to reconsider the layout itself.

If space permits, creating wider pathways and reducing unnecessary obstacles can make the bathroom easier to move through. An open layout may also provide greater flexibility if mobility aids are ever needed.

This doesn’t necessarily mean dramatically increasing the bathroom’s footprint. Sometimes thoughtful placement of the shower, vanity, toilet, and doors can improve circulation without adding square footage.

A professional bathroom designer can help identify opportunities within the existing space.

 

8. Choose Easy-to-Operate Fixtures

Small design decisions can have a big effect on usability.

Lever-style faucet handles, handheld showerheads, easy-to-reach shower controls, and simple cabinet hardware may be easier to operate than fixtures requiring a tight grip or twisting motion.

When selecting fixtures, think beyond how they look today. Consider how easily they could be operated by someone experiencing reduced grip strength or limited range of motion.

Good universal design often benefits everyone in the household, not just older adults.

 

What Is an Aging-in-Place Bathroom?

An aging-in-place bathroom is designed to remain comfortable, functional, and accessible as a homeowner’s needs change over time.

Common features may include a low-threshold shower, grab bars, slip-resistant flooring, improved lighting, comfort-height fixtures, accessible storage, and wider pathways.

Importantly, homeowners don’t need to wait until accessibility becomes a necessity to incorporate these features. Planning during a remodel can make future modifications easier while creating a bathroom that works better today.

 

Can an Accessible Bathroom Still Look High-End?

Absolutely.

Accessible bathroom design has changed significantly. Many of today’s aging-in-place features can be incorporated seamlessly into modern, transitional, traditional, or spa-inspired bathrooms.

Decorative grab bars can coordinate with plumbing fixtures. Walk-in showers can feature frameless glass and custom tile. Accessible vanities can still include beautiful cabinetry and countertops.

The goal is to create a bathroom that supports long-term use without making accessibility the defining visual feature of the room.

 

Should You Plan for Aging in Place Before You Need It?

In many cases, yes.

If you’re already undertaking a major bathroom renovation, it can be easier and more cost-effective to incorporate certain features during construction rather than modifying the finished bathroom later.

For example, wall reinforcement for future grab bars can be installed while walls are open. Shower thresholds can be designed appropriately from the start, and lighting, storage, door placement, and fixture heights can all be considered during the planning phase.

The Bath Remodeling Center’s bathroom remodeling process includes in-home measurements, showroom design and planning, material selections, and professional installation, allowing accessibility considerations to be addressed as part of the overall design.

 

Plan an Accessible Bathroom Remodel in Durham & the Triangle

A bathroom remodel is an opportunity to think beyond today’s design trends and create a space that will continue working for you well into the future.

For homeowners in Durham, Chapel Hill, Hillsborough, Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Wake Forest, and surrounding areas, features like low-threshold showers, improved lighting, thoughtful storage, grab bars, and accessible layouts can help make a bathroom safer and more comfortable without sacrificing style.

The Bath Remodeling Center specializes in custom bathroom renovations throughout the Triangle and offers a 5,000-square-foot design center in Cary where homeowners can explore tile, cabinetry, fixtures, countertops, shower options, and other materials in person.

When you’re ready to start planning, contact The Bath Remodeling Center to discuss an aging-in-place bathroom remodel designed around your home, lifestyle, and long-term needs.

Avoid These Common Bathroom Remodeling Mistakes - How The Bath Remodeling Center Helps

 

 

A bathroom remodel can improve daily comfort, update an outdated home, create more storage, and make the space safer and easier to use. It can also become one of the most frustrating home projects when design decisions are rushed, measurements are inaccurate, materials are selected without considering moisture, or different contractors are left to coordinate the work independently.

For homeowners in Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Morrisville, Holly Springs, Wake Forest, and surrounding Triangle communities, careful planning is especially important. A successful bathroom remodel must balance appearance with ventilation, waterproofing, storage, lighting, accessibility, plumbing, and long-term maintenance.

The Bath Remodeling Center helps homeowners manage those decisions from the initial design consultation through installation. Its Cary-based team provides custom bathroom remodeling services that may include cabinetry, tile, frameless showers, fixtures, countertops, heated floors, tubs, and other finishes tailored to the homeowner’s space and preferences.

Here are some of the most common bathroom remodeling mistakes—and how working with an experienced remodeling team can help you avoid them.

Mistake 1: Beginning Without a Complete Bathroom Remodeling Plan

One of the biggest remodeling mistakes is beginning demolition before the full scope of the project has been decided.

Homeowners may know that they want a larger shower, a new vanity, or updated tile, but those choices are only part of the plan. A complete bathroom design should also account for plumbing locations, electrical needs, lighting placement, storage, ventilation, waterproofing, fixture clearances, door movement, flooring transitions, and how the room will be used every day.

Changes made after construction begins can affect the schedule and budget. Moving a vanity may require relocating plumbing and electrical connections. Choosing a different shower system may affect valve placement, framing, waterproofing, and tile installation. Adding a lighted mirror or heated flooring may require electrical planning that should have been completed before walls and floors were closed.

The Bath Remodeling Center helps homeowners work through these details during the design and planning stage rather than treating each selection as a separate decision. Its bathroom remodeling services guide clients from design through installation, helping create a more coordinated project and a bathroom that works as well as it looks.

Mistake 2: Choosing Looks Over Function

It is easy to become focused on inspiration photos, tile colors, vanity styles, and trending finishes. Those details matter, but a beautiful bathroom can still be disappointing if it lacks storage, has poor lighting, feels cramped, or is difficult to clean.

A floating vanity may look modern, but it must provide enough storage for the household. A dramatic freestanding tub may become the room’s focal point, but it may not be the best use of space if the family rarely takes baths. An oversized shower can feel luxurious, but not if it leaves too little room around the toilet or vanity.

The best bathroom remodels begin with how the room needs to function. Consider who uses the bathroom, whether two people get ready at the same time, how many products need to be stored, whether children or older adults use the space, and how much cleaning and maintenance the homeowner is willing to perform.

The Bath Remodeling Center offers design consultation and custom options so homeowners do not have to choose between style and practicality. Visiting the company’s Cary bathroom showroom also allows homeowners to compare materials, fixtures, cabinetry, tile, and other finishes in person instead of trying to make every decision from small online images.

Mistake 3: Ignoring Bathroom Ventilation

Bathrooms produce a significant amount of moisture. Without sufficient ventilation, that moisture may collect on walls, ceilings, mirrors, cabinets, and other surfaces.

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency explains that bathroom ventilation is particularly important because it removes unwanted moisture and helps limit conditions that support mold and mildew growth. The EPA recommends verifying that the bathroom fan is not merely running, but is actually exhausting enough air from the room.

A common remodeling mistake is spending heavily on decorative finishes while leaving an undersized, noisy, or poorly vented exhaust fan in place. In some homes, the fan may discharge into an attic rather than outdoors, which simply moves the moisture problem to another part of the house.

Ventilation should be reviewed during the planning stage. The right solution depends on the room’s size, ceiling height, shower configuration, existing duct route, and how frequently the bathroom is used. A quieter fan may also encourage family members to use it consistently.

For Cary and Raleigh homeowners, proper moisture management is particularly important during North Carolina’s humid months. A well-designed bathroom should control the moisture created inside the room rather than relying on the HVAC system or an open door to remove it.

Mistake 4: Underestimating Waterproofing

Tile and grout are often mistaken for the waterproof layer of a shower. Although they provide a durable finished surface, the underlying shower assembly must be properly prepared to keep water from reaching framing, subflooring, and adjacent rooms.

Waterproofing mistakes can remain hidden until homeowners notice loose tile, discolored grout, musty odors, stained ceilings, damaged flooring, or deteriorated drywall. By then, repairing the problem may require removing finished materials to reach the source.

The shower base, walls, niches, corners, transitions, curb, drain, and penetrations around fixtures all require careful installation. Even small errors can allow moisture to move behind the visible surfaces.

The EPA emphasizes that moisture control is central to preventing mold and advises homeowners to correct leaks and dry wet materials quickly.

This is one reason bathroom remodeling should involve trained installers rather than a collection of disconnected cosmetic updates. The Bath Remodeling Center uses experienced craftspeople and manages the project as a complete renovation, helping ensure that the hidden construction behind the tile receives as much attention as the finished design.

Mistake 5: Selecting Materials That Are Difficult to Maintain

A material can look beautiful in a showroom while requiring more upkeep than the homeowner expects.

Small mosaic tiles may create an attractive shower floor, but they also introduce more grout lines. Natural stone can offer a distinctive appearance but may require sealing and specialized cleaning. Highly polished floors can become slippery when wet. Dark fixtures may reveal water spots, while certain vanity finishes may show fingerprints or moisture damage more readily.

There is no universally correct bathroom material. The right choice depends on the household’s priorities, including style, durability, cleaning habits, water quality, budget, and expected length of ownership.

Homeowners should compare tile with larger-format panels, framed with frameless shower doors, and standard cabinetry with custom storage solutions. The goal is to understand both the initial appearance and the long-term maintenance requirements before making a final selection.

The Bath Remodeling Center’s showroom gives homeowners an opportunity to see and compare products before committing to them. The company offers access to tile, cabinetry, fixtures, countertops, showers, tubs, and other bathroom finishes, allowing the design to be assembled as a coordinated whole.

Mistake 6: Failing to Plan Enough Storage

Storage is often sacrificed during bathroom design because it is less visually exciting than tile or fixtures. Once the remodel is complete, however, insufficient storage quickly becomes a daily frustration.

A bathroom may need space for towels, toiletries, cleaning products, grooming tools, medications, toilet paper, laundry, and personal items. A beautiful vanity with limited drawers may create countertop clutter. A recessed medicine cabinet may be more useful than a decorative mirror in a smaller room. Shower niches should be sized and positioned according to the products that will actually be stored inside them.

Custom cabinetry can help homeowners use narrow walls, awkward corners, or unused vertical space more effectively. Drawer organizers, tall linen cabinets, built-in niches, and vanities designed around plumbing locations can improve functionality without making the room feel crowded.

Because The Bath Remodeling Center offers custom cabinetry as part of its services, storage can be integrated into the design rather than added after the room is complete.

Mistake 7: Keeping an Inefficient Layout Simply Because It Already Exists

Leaving every fixture in its original location can reduce remodeling costs, but it is not always the best long-term decision.

An older bathroom may have a door that blocks the vanity, a cramped shower beside an unused tub, inadequate clearance around the toilet, or a long vanity that consumes valuable floor space without providing useful storage.

Keeping the layout may be sensible when the room already works well. When it does not, homeowners should at least explore alternative configurations before assuming that the existing plumbing locations must dictate the new design.

Moving plumbing can increase project complexity, so the potential improvement should be weighed against the additional cost. A thoughtful designer can help determine whether rearranging fixtures will meaningfully improve movement, storage, accessibility, or resale appeal.

The Bath Remodeling Center provides in-home measurements and design planning to help homeowners understand what is possible within the existing footprint.

Mistake 8: Forgetting About Lighting

A single ceiling fixture is rarely enough for a well-designed bathroom.

Bathrooms need general lighting for the entire room, focused lighting around the mirror, and sometimes additional lighting in the shower, near a tub, or inside storage areas. Poor fixture placement can create shadows across the face, making everyday grooming more difficult.

Natural light should also be considered. A window can make the room feel larger and brighter, but privacy and moisture-resistant finishes must be addressed. In a windowless bathroom, layered lighting and reflective surfaces can help prevent the space from feeling enclosed.

Dimmer controls can make the bathroom more versatile, providing bright light in the morning and softer illumination in the evening. Lighted mirrors and under-cabinet lighting may also improve both function and appearance.

Electrical planning should happen before construction begins so switches, fixtures, outlets, mirrors, cabinetry, and tile patterns work together.

Mistake 9: Overlooking Accessibility and Future Needs

Homeowners do not have to create an institutional-looking bathroom to make it safer and easier to use.

A low-threshold or curbless shower, wider doorway, handheld showerhead, built-in bench, improved lighting, slip-resistant flooring, and reinforced walls for future grab bars can all increase usability while maintaining a modern appearance.

Even younger homeowners may appreciate features that make the bathroom easier to navigate during an injury, illness, pregnancy, or temporary mobility limitation. For homeowners planning to remain in the property long term, adding adaptable design features during a remodel is usually easier than modifying a finished bathroom later.

A tub-to-shower conversion may also improve accessibility for homeowners who find stepping over a high tub wall difficult. The design should still account for household needs, resale considerations, shower storage, waterproofing, and door placement.

Mistake 10: Removing Every Bathtub Without Considering Resale or Household Needs

Walk-in showers are popular, and many homeowners rarely use a traditional bathtub. Converting an underused tub into a larger shower can be a worthwhile improvement, especially in a primary bathroom.

The mistake is removing every bathtub from the house without considering who may use the home in the future. Families with small children often value having at least one tub, and some buyers may view a house without any bathtub as less practical.

That does not mean every primary bathroom needs one. The decision should be based on the home’s overall layout, the number of bathrooms, homeowner preferences, available space, and likely future use.

The Bath Remodeling Center can help homeowners compare the benefits of a larger shower, shower-and-tub combination, freestanding tub, or tub-to-shower conversion before finalizing the layout.

Mistake 11: Setting an Unrealistic Bathroom Remodeling Budget

Homeowners sometimes create a budget based only on the visible products they plan to purchase. A complete bathroom remodel may also involve demolition, disposal, design, plumbing, electrical work, framing, waterproofing, ventilation, installation labor, permits, repairs, and unforeseen conditions behind the walls.

Our master bathroom remodeling cost guide explains how project scope, material selections and allowances affect the estimate, with a checklist for comparing proposals.

A more reliable budget should reflect the complete scope rather than the price of tile and fixtures alone. Homeowners should also reserve funds for conditions that may not be visible before demolition, such as deteriorated subflooring, previous water damage, outdated plumbing, or inadequate electrical wiring.

Clear plans and written contracts help homeowners understand what is included, what could trigger an additional charge, and how changes will be handled.

Mistake 12: Chasing Trends That May Quickly Feel Outdated

Trends can provide inspiration, but relying too heavily on them may result in a bathroom that feels dated sooner than expected.

Bold patterned tile, highly specific fixture finishes, dramatic colors, and unusual layouts may fit the homeowner’s personality perfectly. The key is to distinguish between features the homeowner genuinely loves and choices being made only because they are currently popular.

A balanced approach often works well: use durable, versatile materials for expensive or difficult-to-replace elements and bring personality into the room through paint, mirrors, lighting, hardware, accessories, or a focused accent area.

Homeowners who expect to remain in the house for many years should prioritize their own preferences. Those planning to sell sooner may benefit from broader, more timeless selections.

Reviewing completed projects in The Bath Remodeling Center’s before-and-after gallery can help homeowners see how different layouts, colors, vanities, showers, and finishes work in real Triangle-area homes.

Mistake 13: Hiring Contractors Who Do Not Manage the Entire Project

Bathroom remodeling involves several trades that must complete their work in the correct order. A delay or communication breakdown between demolition, plumbing, electrical, drywall, waterproofing, tile, cabinetry, glass, and fixture installation can affect the entire project.

When homeowners hire each trade separately, they may become responsible for scheduling, material coordination, quality control, and resolving disagreements about who is responsible for a problem.

A full-service bathroom remodeling company provides a more coordinated process. The Bath Remodeling Center handles design, product selection, measurements, planning, and installation, helping homeowners work with one team rather than managing multiple disconnected providers. The company is also a North Carolina-licensed general contractor and reports more than 25 years of experience serving the area.

Mistake 14: Ordering Materials Before Final Measurements and Design Approval

Ordering tile, cabinets, shower glass, countertops, or fixtures too early may lead to incorrect quantities, incompatible products, or materials that do not fit the final layout.

Custom shower glass must be measured after the surrounding surfaces are installed. Vanities must coordinate with plumbing locations, wall dimensions, mirrors, lighting, and door clearances. Tile quantities should account for room dimensions, pattern, cuts, breakage, and future repairs.

Homeowners should finalize the layout and confirm measurements before placing major orders. A coordinated design and installation team can also check compatibility among products, which is especially important when fixtures and finishes come from different manufacturers.

Mistake 15: Focusing Only on the Lowest Estimate

Bathroom remodeling estimates can differ because they include different scopes, materials, construction methods, warranty coverage, and levels of project management.

A low estimate may exclude demolition, disposal, plumbing modifications, electrical work, permits, waterproofing, painting, shower glass, or repairs discovered after the project begins. Another estimate may appear higher because it accounts for the complete renovation.

Before comparing prices, homeowners should compare what is actually included. Written proposals should identify the products, labor, responsibilities, allowances, project stages, payment terms, and process for handling changes.

The lowest initial price does not always create the lowest total project cost. Correcting poor waterproofing, damaged tile, inaccurate cabinetry, or improperly installed fixtures can be far more expensive than completing the work correctly the first time.

How The Bath Remodeling Center Helps Cary Homeowners Avoid These Mistakes

The Bath Remodeling Center approaches bathroom remodeling as a coordinated design-and-build process.

The team begins by understanding the homeowner’s goals, measuring the space, reviewing layout options, and helping select fixtures and finishes. Homeowners can explore products at the company’s approximately 5,000-square-foot showroom in Downtown Cary, where they can compare tile, cabinetry, countertops, bath products, and other materials in person.

Once the design is established, the company’s installation team manages the physical renovation. This integrated process helps reduce conflicts among measurements, materials, trades, and scheduling.

The company’s services include custom vanities, frameless showers, tile, tubs, heated floors, shower valves, faucets, granite countertops, and other bathroom features. It serves homeowners throughout Cary, Raleigh, Apex, and other Triangle communities.

Frequently Asked Questions About Bathroom Remodeling
What should I decide first when planning a bathroom remodel?

Begin with the room’s functional needs and the problems you want the remodel to solve. Establish the preferred layout, shower or tub configuration, storage needs, accessibility goals, and approximate budget before focusing on decorative details.

How long does a bathroom remodel take?

The timeline depends on the project’s size, complexity, material availability, inspections, and whether plumbing or structural changes are required. The Bath Remodeling Center states that many of its custom bathroom projects can be completed within approximately 10 to 13 days once installation begins, although individual projects may vary.

Is it worth changing the bathroom layout?

A layout change may be worthwhile when it significantly improves movement, shower size, storage, privacy, or accessibility. If the existing layout works well, maintaining plumbing locations may help control costs.

Should I choose bathroom materials online or in a showroom?

Online research is helpful for gathering ideas, but a showroom makes it easier to evaluate color, texture, scale, quality, and how multiple materials look together. It can also reduce the risk of ordering incompatible products.

How can I prevent moisture problems after remodeling?

A bathroom needs appropriate waterproofing, properly installed plumbing, moisture-resistant materials, and adequate ventilation. The exhaust fan should vent outdoors and be sized to remove moisture effectively.

Do I need a general contractor for a bathroom remodel?

A minor cosmetic update may not require the same coordination as a complete renovation. A full bathroom remodel involving plumbing, electrical work, waterproofing, cabinetry, tile, and multiple trades is generally easier to manage through a licensed contractor overseeing the complete project.

Plan a Better Bathroom Remodel in Cary, NC

A successful bathroom remodel is not simply a collection of attractive products. It is a carefully planned space in which the layout, ventilation, waterproofing, storage, lighting, plumbing, and finishes work together.

Avoiding common remodeling mistakes begins with asking the right questions before demolition starts. Homeowners should understand the full project scope, compare materials in person, plan for moisture and future needs, and work with a qualified team that can coordinate the renovation from design through installation.

The Bath Remodeling Center helps homeowners in Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Morrisville, Holly Springs, Wake Forest, and surrounding Triangle communities create bathrooms that are functional, attractive, and designed around the way they live.

Master Bath Remodel Checklist: What to Know Before You Start in Wake Forest

 

 

A master bathroom remodel is one of the most rewarding home improvement projects you can take on. It can make your daily routine easier, improve storage, upgrade comfort, and create a more relaxing space inside your Wake Forest home. But before choosing tile, vanities, fixtures, and finishes, it is important to start with a clear plan.

For homeowners in Wake Forest, Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Durham, and surrounding areas, a successful master bath remodel begins with understanding your goals, budget, timeline, layout, materials, and contractor selection. This checklist can help you prepare before your project begins.

 

Start With How You Use the Space

Before focusing on design inspiration, think about how your current bathroom works and where it falls short. Maybe the shower feels too small, the tub is rarely used, the vanity does not offer enough storage, or the lighting makes the space feel dark. Some homeowners want a spa-like retreat, while others need a more practical layout for busy mornings.

A master bath remodel should solve everyday problems, not just update the look of the room. The more specific you are about what is not working now, the easier it will be to create a bathroom that feels custom to your lifestyle.

 

Decide What Type of Remodel You Need

Not every master bathroom project requires the same scope. Some homeowners need a cosmetic refresh with updated tile, fixtures, lighting, and countertops. Others want a full remodel that changes the layout, replaces the shower or tub, upgrades flooring, improves storage, and creates a more functional design.

The Bath Remodeling Center specializes in bath remodeling for homeowners who want a more functional and beautiful bathroom. Their services include custom-built vanities, frameless showers, tubs, heated floors, tile selections, faucets, shower valves, countertops, and more.

 

Set a Realistic Budget Early

Budget planning is one of the most important steps in any remodel. Costs can vary depending on the size of the bathroom, the quality of materials, the complexity of the design, and whether plumbing or electrical changes are needed.

A larger master bath remodel may include upgraded tile, custom cabinetry, frameless glass, new fixtures, improved lighting, heated flooring, and layout changes. Planning your budget early helps guide design decisions and reduces surprises once the project begins.

If you are still researching price ranges, The Bath Remodeling Center’s guide on how much it costs to remodel a master bathroom explains project scopes, allowances and the items to compare in written estimates. Use it to prepare questions before committing to a budget.

 

Think Carefully About Layout

A beautiful bathroom still needs to function well. Before you commit to a layout, consider traffic flow, door swings, vanity spacing, shower size, toilet placement, and storage access. In many Wake Forest homes, the biggest opportunity is improving how the existing square footage is used.

You may not need to move every plumbing line to create a better experience. Sometimes a larger shower, a better vanity configuration, updated lighting, or smarter storage can completely change how the room feels. In other cases, a more involved layout change may be worth the investment if it makes the space easier to use every day.

 

Choose Materials That Fit North Carolina Homes

Bathrooms in North Carolina need materials that can handle moisture, humidity, daily cleaning, and long-term use. Tile, grout, waterproof flooring, countertops, cabinetry, and shower systems should be selected for both appearance and performance.

While trends can be inspiring, durability matters. A master bath should be designed to look beautiful now and hold up well for years. The Bath Remodeling Center’s showroom gallery is a helpful place to explore design inspiration, finishes, and completed project examples.

 

Prioritize Shower and Tub Decisions

One of the biggest decisions in a master bath remodel is whether to keep a tub, replace it, remove it, or expand the shower. Many homeowners are choosing larger walk-in showers with glass enclosures, built-in niches, benches, and upgraded fixtures. Others still prefer a soaking tub for relaxation or resale appeal.

There is no single right answer. The best choice depends on your lifestyle, your home’s layout, and how you plan to use the space. If you rarely use the tub and want a more spacious shower, a tub-to-shower conversion may make sense. If the bathroom has enough space, keeping both may offer the best balance.

 

Plan for Water-Efficient Fixtures

A remodel is a smart time to upgrade to more efficient plumbing fixtures. Water-saving faucets, showerheads, and toilets can help reduce water use without sacrificing performance.

The EPA WaterSense program notes that WaterSense labeled bathroom sink faucets and accessories use a maximum of 1.5 gallons per minute and can reduce flow by 30 percent or more compared with standard models. You can learn more from the EPA’s guide to Bathroom Faucets.

Choosing efficient fixtures during your remodel can support long-term savings and make your bathroom more environmentally responsible.

 

Do Not Overlook Lighting and Ventilation

Lighting can make a master bath feel brighter, cleaner, and more comfortable. A well-designed bathroom often includes layered lighting, such as overhead lights, vanity lighting, and accent lighting near the shower or tub.

Ventilation is just as important. Bathrooms produce moisture every day, and poor ventilation can contribute to foggy mirrors, lingering humidity, and potential moisture damage. During the planning phase, make sure ventilation is part of the conversation, especially if your current bathroom feels humid or stuffy.

 

Visit a Showroom Before Finalizing Choices

Seeing materials in person can make a big difference. Tile, countertops, hardware, glass, and cabinet finishes often look different in a showroom than they do online. Visiting a showroom can help you compare textures, colors, and combinations more confidently.

The Bath Remodeling Center invites homeowners to visit its Cary showroom, where they can explore premium bath and tile products and get inspiration for their remodel.

 

Choose an Experienced Bathroom Remodeling Team

A master bath remodel involves design, construction, tile work, fixtures, finishes, and careful coordination. Choosing an experienced remodeling company can help keep the project organized and reduce costly mistakes.

The Bath Remodeling Center is based in Cary and serves homeowners across the surrounding area with bathroom renovation services. Their team focuses on transforming outdated or dysfunctional bathrooms into functional, stylish, and relaxing spaces.

 

Schedule Your Master Bath Remodel Consultation

A successful master bath remodel starts long before demolition begins. By thinking through your goals, budget, layout, materials, fixtures, storage, lighting, and contractor selection, you can feel more confident about the process and the final result.

If you are planning a master bath remodel in Wake Forest, Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Durham, or a nearby community, The Bath Remodeling Center can help you create a bathroom that fits your home and lifestyle.

Contact The Bath Remodeling Center today to schedule a consultation and start planning your master bathroom remodel.

What Should I Look for When Searching “Bath Remodeling Near Me” in Cary, NC?

 

 

 

When homeowners start thinking about updating an outdated, cramped, or worn-down bathroom, one of the first searches they usually make is “bath remodeling near me.” It makes sense — bathroom remodeling is a big investment, and you want a local company that understands your home, your style, your budget, and the needs of homeowners in Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Durham, Chapel Hill, and the surrounding Triangle area.

But once the search results come up, how do you know which bathroom remodeling company is the right choice?

If you’re planning a bathroom renovation in Cary, NC or nearby, here are the most important things to look for before choosing a remodeler.

 

1. Look for a Local Bathroom Remodeling Company With Real Experience

Not all remodeling companies specialize in bathrooms. A bathroom remodel requires careful planning, design knowledge, plumbing coordination, ventilation considerations, waterproofing, tile work, cabinetry, fixtures, and finishes. That’s why it helps to choose a company that focuses specifically on bathroom transformations.

The Bath Remodeling Center provides custom bath remodeling services in Cary, NC for homeowners who want a bathroom that feels more functional, beautiful, and personalized. Their team works with homeowners throughout Cary, Raleigh, Apex, and nearby areas to create bathrooms that fit each client’s needs and style.

 

2. Choose a Remodeler That Offers Design Support

A successful bathroom remodel is about more than replacing old materials. The layout, storage, shower design, lighting, tile, fixtures, and finishes all need to work together.

That’s why design support is so important. Homeowners should look for a remodeler that can help them compare materials, talk through style options, and make confident decisions before the project begins.

The Bath Remodeling Center’s Cary bathroom showroom gives homeowners the opportunity to see and touch materials in person, explore bathroom vignettes, and gather inspiration for their remodel. This can make the process much easier than trying to choose everything from photos online.

 

3. Ask About the Remodeling Process

When you search “bath remodeling near me,” you’re not just looking for beautiful photos — you’re looking for a company that can guide the project from start to finish.

A good bathroom remodeler should be able to explain:

How the consultation works
How design selections are made
How budgeting is handled
What happens before installation begins
How long the project may take
Who will be communicating with you throughout the process

The Bath Remodeling Center’s bathroom remodeling process is built around helping homeowners plan their renovation with clear expectations, personalized support, and competitive, fair pricing.

 

4. Review Before-and-After Bathroom Remodels

Before hiring a bathroom remodeling company, take time to look at real project examples. Before-and-after photos can help you understand the company’s design style, craftsmanship, attention to detail, and ability to transform different bathroom sizes and layouts.

The Bath Remodeling Center features a before-and-after bathroom remodel gallery where homeowners can see examples of small bathroom remodels, larger transformations, and updated bathroom designs completed by their team.

 

5. Make Sure Your Bathroom Remodel Is Built for Long-Term Function

A beautiful bathroom should also work well for everyday life. That means thinking through practical details like storage, shower access, lighting, ventilation, surface durability, and ease of cleaning.

Ventilation is especially important in a bathroom remodel. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency notes that bathroom ventilation helps remove unwanted moisture and can help prevent mold and mildew growth.

When working with a professional bathroom remodeling team, homeowners can talk through design and function together — so the final result looks great and performs well over time.

 

6. Pick a Company That Understands Cary and Triangle-Area Homes

Local experience matters. Homes in Cary and the surrounding Triangle area vary widely, from older homes with dated bathrooms to newer homes that need more personalized, high-end updates. A local remodeling company will understand common layouts, local homeowner preferences, and what works well for the area.

The Bath Remodeling Center serves homeowners across Cary and nearby communities. You can view their bathroom remodeling service areas to see where their team provides bathroom renovation services throughout the region.

 

Is It Time to Start Your Bathroom Remodel?

If you’ve been searching “bath remodeling near me” because your bathroom feels outdated, lacks storage, has an awkward layout, or simply no longer matches your style, now may be the right time to start planning.

The Bath Remodeling Center helps homeowners create bathrooms that are stylish, functional, and tailored to their needs. From design consultation and material selection to installation and finishing details, their team provides full-service support for bathroom remodeling projects in Cary, NC and the surrounding Triangle area.

Whether you’re dreaming of a spa-inspired primary bathroom, a modern shower upgrade, a more functional guest bath, or a complete bathroom transformation, The Bath Remodeling Center can help bring your vision to life.

 

Schedule a Bathroom Remodeling Consultation in Cary, NC

When you’re ready to move beyond searching “bath remodeling near me,” connect with a trusted local team that specializes in custom bathroom renovations. The Bath Remodeling Center offers expert craftsmanship, personalized design support, and a showroom experience that helps make the remodeling process easier from the start.

Contact The Bath Remodeling Center today to start planning your bathroom remodel in Cary, NC and the surrounding area.
